newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid's Barajas airport shut due lighting failure.
newsitem.headline: Madrid's Barajas airport shut due lighting failure.

text.p: Madrid's main airport Barajas closed down on Tuesday evening when the runway lighting system failed due to a fire in electrical cables, Spanish media reported.
The airport was not expected to open again until Wednesday morning at 0730 GMT, the Spanish news agency Efe reported.
Airport spokesmen were not immediately available for comment.
The lights went out after a fire in electrical cables in one of the airport corridors which produced large columns of smoke, Efe said.
Barajas has been suffering severe delays in the last two months, prompting the airports authority AENA to enforce strict limits on the number of flights arriving and departing.
The airport is Spain's busiest and handles around 20 million passengers a year.
